### D492 — GYLDENDAL: TOKEN FIRST, URL SECOND, ONE TRANSACTION — AND THE CORRECTED CRITERION IS STILL WRONG.

41 days live, unremediated, and it **changed phase during this wave**. `unreachable` **stops dead at
2026-08-09 07:22:01** (458 rows from 08-04) and `unauthorized` **starts at 07:37:01** — the very next tick —
and every tick since is `unauthorized` (11 rows to 10:07:00). Per `usage.ex`'s own comment, `unauthorized` is
proof the bearer **reached and was EVALUATED** by another tenant's app layer. The platform has been in the
provably-worse phase for the whole of this wave. `dig` → `116.203.98.0` (row f5e1392e's box), which answers
302; yo's own box `167.233.194.23` answers 000. **Misdelivery is 100%.**

**THE ORDERING RULING IS CONFIRMED ON LIVE DATA, and D457's line cites are stale** (`provisioning_fqdn_claim/1`
is at `registry.ex:5501`, not 5416-7). The function's only row filter is `where([b], b.url == ^url)` (`:5507`).
Rows matching that url excluding b1259514 = **0**, so nulling `url` first leaves the query empty and
`Enum.find_value(:free, &claim_leg/2)` returns `:free` **with no leg evaluated** — `:admin_credential` disarmed
by erasure of its own input. Token-first is safe by contrast: with the token gone the next legs still fire
(`recent_sample=t → :recent_usage_sample`; `live_sub=t → :active_subscription`). **NULL the token FIRST, the
url SECOND, one BEGIN/COMMIT.** Use NULL, never a repoint — `barkparks_url_unique_idx` is UNIQUE on url WHERE
NOT NULL. Rotate yo's instance admin token; treat it as disclosed.

**REFINEMENT that softens D457's generalization without weakening the order:** `provisioning_fqdn_claim/1`'s
ONLY caller is `custom_host_taken?/2` (`:5415-5420`), a fail-closed OR of four surfaces, and
`other_barkpark_custom_host?` **already refuses** this name because row f5e1392e holds it as `custom_host`. So
`:free` is not, today, a live path to handing the name away. The ordering is load-bearing for the CREDENTIAL
window, not for the name. State it as the structural finding it is or it is refutable.

**AND THE CORRECTED PACKET'S CRITERION 2 IS STILL PROBABLY UNSATISFIABLE.** The incumbent's criterion 3
("`usage_samples` shows no new row for b1259514") is unsatisfiable because the sweep is **host-keyed**
(`checkable_scope/1`, `registry.ex:3813-3815` — url is never consulted) and `record_sample/1`
(`usage.ex:424-432`) inserts unconditionally; b1259514's host survives the fix, so rows keep landing every 15
minutes. But the draft's correction — "ZERO new rows carry `unavailable_reason`" — **also fails on a working
fix**: `:not_live` is not a member of `@unavailable_reasons` (`usage.ex:161-162`), so the post-fix envelope
falls through to `"unknown"` at `:257`. **RULING: the criterion is "no new row carries a DELIVERY-PROVING
reason (`unreachable|unauthorized|refused|instance_error`)."** D475's unblock stands unchanged: the w25
incumbent is still `published` (rev `80239efd7c09c965d3837f2c7e1f5eef`), so the E4 dedup wall is still armed —

### D496 — THE 81% BEHIND IS A CLOSED PRE-WRITER BACKLOG. THE LIVE DEFECT IS `WRONG=1`, AND WAVE 28 MANUFACTURED IT AGAINST ITSELF.

Two decisive runs of `scripts/crown-reconcile.sh` from origin/main's tree against live production, 12:06Z:

```
--window-hours 24 : VERDICT: NOT reconciled — behind=17/21 delivering runs, wrong=1/28 rows, serving-unrecorded=0.
--window-hours  3 : VERDICT: NOT reconciled — behind=0/4  delivering runs, wrong=1/28 rows, serving-unrecorded=0.
```

**behind=0/4. Zero post-fix runs are silent.** And the boundary is not the one anybody named: the
`record-delivery` job — the only thing that writes `platform_deliveries` from inside a run — came into
existence at **2026-08-09T09:39:44Z via #11167 (`67f4a6ab2`)**, not at 11:34:36Z via #11203. All 17 BEHIND runs
were created 2026-08-08T12:27:30Z..2026-08-09T08:39:42Z, the newest **three hours before the writer existed**,
and their `jobs` arrays do not contain the recorder in any state — not `skipped`, **absent**. There was no gate
to fail; there was no job. Since 09:39:44Z: three delivering runs, three recorded, 100%, plus one docs-only run
that correctly recorded nothing and one run 16 seconds pre-writer whose sha rides as a `carried` row.

**RULING: no backfill is required for correctness and no recorder-gate is dropping deliveries.** But the gate
reds every 6h until ~2026-08-10T08:40Z on history it cannot change, and **a gate that cannot go green teaches
people to ignore it** — the same alarm that just produced the genuine finding. **RULING: a run created before
the recorder's birth is reported as its own named class, PREDATES-WRITER, with its own count and the birth
instant printed — never as BEHIND, and never silently dropped by a narrowed window.** The exemption is a
denominator, not a hiding place.

**`WRONG=1` is a FALSE ACCUSATION, and it is the epic's own newest alarm accusing the epic's own newest
recorder.** `8e83b709a` is a real, correct row: #11203 makes the recorder write the sha the BOX WAS SERVING as
the primary `carried=f` row, and run 31311142804 stored its own trigger sha `5f3813659` as `carried=t`.
`crown-reconcile.sh` builds its alibi set from delivering-run **HEAD shas** (`:397-404`) and accuses any
non-carried row absent from it (`:461`), exempting only `carried` rows (`:49-51`). #11203 INVERTED that premise
four minutes before #11205 merged and neither PR read the other. `8e83b709a` never had a `deploy.yml` run of
its own (concurrency coalescing — `5f38` and `8e83` merged 13 seconds apart, `5f38` an ancestor of `8e83`), so
the alibi set structurally CANNOT contain it. It fired on 1 of the 4 recent delivering runs.

**RULING: the alibi is `delivering_run_id`, not the head sha.** A non-carried row is legitimate iff its
`delivering_run_id` is in the delivering set. The field is already on BOTH read paths — `PlatformDelivery.to_json/1`
(`platform_delivery.ex:448`) and the SQL fallback's own SELECT (`crown-reconcile.sh:252`) — so no migration and
no route change; the jq at `:443` already parses the payload and simply does not ask for the field. **Keep the
headSha comparison ONLY as the fallback when `delivering_run_id` is absent**, so the `carried: null →
UNCLASSIFIED` discipline (`:456`) survives and an unmeasured row still cannot be counted clean. **And the
mutation case MUST mutate `delivering_run_id`, not only the sha** — today's case (c) mutates the sha alone and
would pass a broken implementation, which would make WRONG unable to lose: the exact failure this epic kills.

BEHIND is immune and must stay so: it asks whether the crown holds ANY row for the sha, carried or not
(`:416`), which is why run 31311142804 was correctly not counted behind. Only WRONG false-accuses.

Three traps for anyone re-running this. **Piping the script EATS its exit code** — a rc=1 verdict printed
`RC=0`; read the VERDICT line, never `$?`. `gh run view` without `-R FRIKKern/barkpark` 404s every id from
outside the checkout. And the `timeout` binary does not exist on this host. **The route is unreachable to CI**:
every poll logged `the route answered HTTP 401 to the WORKER principal — read via the control plane's postgres
container instead`, `CR_VIA=sql` — which answers #11201 on live data, in both CI and a local re-run: the
postgres fallback is the ONLY working path, and if it is ever removed none of these readings are reproducible.

**The population is thin and the verdict must say so.** Only three strictly-post-writer delivering runs exist.
3/3 is a real 100% but a thin one, and the WRONG row ages out of the 24h window tomorrow — it RECURS, it does
not persist. A later wave that measures once and sees 0 must not call it fixed.

### D498 — `max` REFUSES ON OPEN WINDOWS AND PRINTS ON CLOSED ONES. THAT IS WORSE THAN NEVER PRINTING.

The direction and the digest both held that `max` can essentially never print. **Half wrong, and the wrong half
is the dangerous half.** Live, 12:02–12:05Z: OPEN windows refuse (24h at 1.0% unresolved, 7d at 0.3%, headroom
`1.0 − 1.0 = 0.0`, so ONE pending row refuses forever). **CLOSED windows PRINT** — 08-06→08-07 max
**43063.476s**, 08-07→08-08 **2500.948s**, 08-08→08-09 **3784.42s**, 08-05→08-08 **47618.033s**, all with
pending=0 and `oldest_pending_seconds` null. Mechanism: `live_marks/1` (`deploy_ledger.ex:1146`) bounds the
covering-live query BELOW and **not above**, so a deferral inside a fully-past window is COVERED by a live build
that happened after the window closed.

**RULING: a criterion reading "p50/p95/max appear" does not MISS by construction — it misses
NON-DETERMINISTICALLY, and can be closed GREEN by choosing the window, then flips on re-read tomorrow. The
criterion is: "p50, p95 and max each appear as a number OR as its named refusal, and the render is read at
`to=now`."** For the same reason a closed-window reading is NOT REPRODUCIBLE (rows only ever move
PENDING→COVERED), so **`as_of` is load-bearing, not decoration**.

**RULING on the render contract** — nothing new, it is D3 + D479 + the shape `main` already ships. Copy
`deployDeliveryValue`; do not invent a second refusal vocabulary (the digest's is `rate_clause/1`,
`digest_email.ex:492`, `UNMEASURED (#{reason})` with the counts surviving). On a refusal print: the label, the
literal token `NO NUMBER`, the control plane's `reason` **verbatim and unedited**, and — always, refused or not
— the population triple `covered / pending / unreadable` out of `deferred`, plus `as_of`. Never an empty cell,
never `0s`, never the label omitted.

**Print `unresolved_fraction` and `headroom` BESIDE the reason, not inside it**, because
`deferral_wait_quantile`'s `cond` puts `n < @min_sample` FIRST and MASKS the identifiability fact: on a 1h
window the reason reads only `sample 23 below min_sample 200` while the same node carries
`unresolved_fraction: 0.2581` against p95's `0.05` headroom — **5.2× over, invisible to a renderer that prints
only `Reason`**. p95 is safe at ≥24h and unsafe at exactly the widths an operator watching a live incident will
type.

`oldest_pending_seconds` is the honest lower-bound stand-in for `max` (`STILL WAITING >= …`, the shape
`deployDeliveryWaiting` already ships) — **with a hole that must close in the same PR**: if the unresolved mass
is entirely UNREADABLE (pending 0, unreadable > 0) then `max` refuses AND the bound is nil, and a naive "if
refused, print the bound" renderer emits an empty cell — a NEW silent mis-report inside the slice built to end
them. That branch prints the UNREADABLE count with its control-plane label. Today `unreadable = 0` on every
window read, denominator **3,138 over 7d as of 12:02:25Z** — a zero counter that prints its denominator and its
as-of, never "no unreadable rows".

**AND THE FLAGSHIP INSTRUMENT'S OWN LAW HAS NO GUARD.** Nothing anywhere pins `deferral_wait`'s zero-headroom
refusal: `wait.max` is asserted at `deploy_ledger_test.exs:2005` (NOT refused), `:2046`, `:2113` — never
`wait.max.refused`; the p95 refusal test at `:2129` says nothing about max. **Mutating
`deferral_wait_quantile(seconds, 1.0, "max", unresolved, …)` → `…, 0, …` — which deletes the law entirely —
passes 76 tests, 0 failures.** The `delivery` node's equivalent law IS pinned (`:2364`). **RULING: the law gets
a test that can lose, proven by re-running that exact mutation and watching it red.**

### D499 — THE DAILY DIGEST SILENTLY SKIPS ~43% OF DAYS AND NOTHING RECORDS THE LOSS.

`DailyDigestWorker` is `{"0 6 * * *"}` (`config/config.exs:334`) with `unique: [period: 86_400]`
(`daily_digest_worker.ex:33`). Oban 2.23.0's unique DEFAULTS are `timestamp: :inserted_at` and
`states: [scheduled, available, executing, retryable, completed]` (`deps/oban/lib/oban/job.ex:232-237`). The
window is therefore a **ROLLING 86,400 seconds off the PREVIOUS job's `inserted_at`**, not a calendar day, and
cron tick jitter is sub-second. Whenever today's tick inserts microseconds EARLIER in the second than
yesterday's, the enqueue is refused as a duplicate: **no oban row, no log, no telemetry, no delivery row,
nothing.** The four surviving rows prove the mechanism exactly:

| day | inserted_at | next day |
|---|---|---|
| 08-04 | 06:00:00.514449 | 08-05 at .710358 > .514449 → allowed |
| 08-05 | 06:00:00.710358 | 08-06 tick landed earlier → **EATEN** |
| 08-07 | 06:00:00.789878 | 08-08 tick landed earlier → **EATEN** |
| 08-09 | 06:00:00.337078 | (08-07's row is outside the 86,400s lookback) |

**08-03, 08-06 and 08-08 have no digest job at all — 3 of 7 days, 43%.** Not pruning: `oban_jobs` retains back
to 2026-08-01 (83,857 rows) and the hourly `TrialExpiryWorker` has 166 rows over the same span, full coverage.
The epic already knows this trap **by name in a different worker** — `dr-w20-refusal-backoff-depth-derived`,
where `@unique states` are `[:available, :scheduled]`, which is precisely why it does NOT bite there and DOES
bite here. **Nothing is filed for the digest.**

**RULING: the digest's `@unique` names its states EXPLICITLY and excludes `:completed`, and the fix ships with
a behavioural test — insert, mark the job `completed`, insert again, demand a SECOND distinct row — proven able
to lose by reverting the opts and watching it red.** This is the wish verbatim: a failure that is both silent
and unreported, sitting inside the epic's own newest reporting instrument, because what is not being sent on
43% of days is #11208's per-team deploy-health block. The mechanism is inferred from four `inserted_at` values
plus documented defaults, not from a mutation — **which is exactly why the slice's proof obligation is the
behavioural test, not a re-reading of Oban's docs.**

Corollary for the record: the digest reached a human **for the first time ever on 2026-08-09**. Only four
`fleet_digest` rows exist in all history (a table retaining since 2026-07-01 that nothing prunes), all at
06:00:00.69–01.11Z that morning; the 08-07 job completed in 10ms and wrote zero deliveries. Three of those four
sends went to zero-site teams receiving the "owns no sites" sentence #11208 added to stop the false alarm —
**75% of this rail's audience.** That half of #11208 is proven live.

### D500 — THE DIGEST'S DEPLOY-HEALTH SENTENCE GAINS THE WAIT, AND WHAT IT MAY NOT CLAIM.

`census.deferral_wait` is **in hand at the call site and thrown away**: `digest_email.ex:301` already calls
`DeployLedger.census(from, now, site_ids: site_ids, site_limit: 0)`, and `window_health/3` (`:295-307`) builds
`%{label, from, to, door, deferred, failed, rate}` with no wait key, so `deploy_line/1` (`:485-487`) still says
only "N deferred by a busy box". Confirmed against **live rendered bytes**, not source: the deployed release
prints `760 attempted, of which 502 deferred by a busy box — 2.37% failed post-door (18 of 760 attempted).` and
no wait statistic anywhere. The fix is one map key and one clause.

**It MUST reuse `window_health/3`.** `deploy_ledger_reachability_test.exs:658` pins `census/3`'s external
caller arity multiset to EXACTLY `[2, 3, 3]`; a fourth call site reds it by design, and hiding one behind a
`DeployLedger` wrapper would hold the multiset and hide the consumer permanently — D493's rubber-stamp-by-evasion.

**D14 is not breached, and this is recorded so a reviewer does not read it as a fence.** D14 forbids "ANOTHER
PER-DEPLOYMENT ALERT PRODUCER" and its own closing clause names a RATE as the sanctioned instrument. D446
already ruled, on this exact file, that editing `digest_email.ex` "is not an 841st email producer; it is an
existing one told to stop lying", and wave 28 listed that fence as honoured while adding +304 lines to it.
D232 states the operative test: "this epic reports ON the rail; it never changes how loudly it sends." A clause
inside an existing sentence changes zero sends. **The D200 tenancy hazard is also absent**: `deferral_wait/2`
reads the same `scoped` query as the rest of the census, bounded by the site ids the deferred rows themselves
carry, so a team's wait can never quote another team's rows.

**`min_sample` is 200 and the digest is TEAM-scoped.** Guerrilla clears it (covered 492 at 24h, 3,132 at 7d); a
small team gets a REFUSAL sentence and a zero-site team never reaches `deploy_line` at all. **A criterion
reading "the digest prints p50" MISSES for most teams.** It reads: **"the digest prints the wait OR the control
plane's own refusal reason, with its population beside it"**, modelled on `rate_clause/1`, which already
carries the counts through a refusal.

**A NEW mislabel, unfiled, found on live rendered bytes and NOT fixed this wave.** The sentence says "% failed
post-door" over a denominator that `@basis_attempted` (`deploy_ledger.ex:335`) explicitly declares INCLUDES the
deferrals. A deferral is the door never opening. The genuinely post-door figure is 18/258 = **6.98%**, ~3× the
2.37% a human reads — and this reconciles the two rates this wave quoted: two bases, only one labelled. It
prints its denominator, so it is not a hidden lie. **Changing the denominator changes every historical
comparison and needs its own ruling on what "post-door" means.** Filed.

### D501 — `dr-w28-s5`'s CRITERION IS UNCLOSABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. HERE IS ITS REPLACEMENT.

`notification_deliveries` has twelve columns and **not one carries content**: `id, team_id, recipient, event,
channel, kind, status, attempts, last_error, inserted_at, updated_at, http_status`. A row proves an address and
a status, never a sentence. `cloud-postfix-1` keeps no maillog and is recreated on every control-plane deploy
(`dr-w26-bl-postfix-recreate-destroys-delivery-proof`, live-confirmed today). **No email body the platform has
ever sent is recoverable anywhere.** **RULING: the criterion is restated as "the deploy-health block's exact
bytes are captured by rendering `DigestEmail.build/2` through the live release's own `Registry` +
`DeployLedger` reads, per team, with the read timestamp quoted"** — which this wave's verify round already
executed for all three real teams. Waiting for the next 06:00Z buys a `status=sent` row and nothing more.
Persisting subject + rendered body (or a body hash plus the numeric block) on the delivery row is filed: today
"the digest said X" can only ever be a claim about source, never about what was sent.

### D502 — THE WATCH'S ONLY GREEN IN ITS ENTIRE LIFE WAS A BLIND RUN.

Census of every `stale-verdict-watch.yml` run ever (19 total): `pull_request` 2/2 success (harness-only job),
`push` 15 → 5 cancelled / 9 failure / **1 success**, `schedule` 2 → 2 failure. **The single push success is run
31311358759 — the run that classified 0 of 39 rows** and printed `ok — no CONFLICTING pull request is asserting
a green required verdict that main has moved past.` **Every green this instrument has ever shown a human was
produced by a run that could not look.** It concluded SUCCESS 68 seconds before a 23-row RED run on the same
tree.

Two independent halves. `stale-verdict-watch.sh:329-335` returns 2 when `.reported == 0 && .unknown > 0`, and
the workflow maps rc=2 to `exit 0` (`:114`). AND `render()` (`:239`) prints the clean sentence on the SOLE
condition `(.reported | length) == 0`, which is empty **because** nothing was classified. **Zero coverage and
perfect coverage are the same branch.**

**Premise correction that changes the criterion:** "printed the clean sentence with no denominator" is NOT
literally true — the POPULATION line two lines above DID print `39 open · 0 CONFLICTING · 0 MERGEABLE · 39
UNKNOWN`, and all 39 were named. The failure is narrower and nastier: the **sentence** is unqualified and the
**conclusion** is SUCCESS, and a human skimming a green check reads only those two. **The criterion is that the
SENTENCE ITSELF carries `classified N of M`, and that the run does not conclude success.**

**RULING: a new exit code 5 = BLIND (`open > 0 AND classified == 0`), plus a workflow arm `5) … exit 1`.** This
ADDS an arm and leaves 1/2/3/4 and their freshly-split sentences byte-identical — #11206's arms are untouched by
construction, not by care. The sentence becomes three-way: `BLIND — classified 0 of N` / `INCONCLUSIVE —
classified K of N … M rows went unread` / `ok — … (classified N of N open)`.

**THE TRAP INSIDE THE FIX.** The predicate is `open > 0 AND classified == 0`, **never** `classified == 0`.
Harness disarm probe (i) — "an empty population exits 0 — the red is conditional, not unconditional" — feeds
`[]`, where classified is also 0. A naive predicate reds unconditionally and fails the probe designed to catch
exactly this. Its only tripwire sits 150 lines away in a section named "disarm"; a builder trimming that
section for speed removes the one thing catching an unconditional red.

**THE COLLISION.** Harness section (d) (`:181-183`) feeds a SINGLE all-UNKNOWN row and asserts `rc = 2`. **That
fixture IS the blind case.** Any correct fix breaks a currently-green assertion of the 53 (measured: `FAIL
expected exit 2, got 5`). **RULING: split section (d) into PARTIAL (add a MERGEABLE row, still exit 2, and the
sentence now carries its coverage) and TOTAL (a new all-UNKNOWN fixture, exit 5).** A builder who does not know
this will either water the fix down to keep the harness green, or break it and be told to revert.

**Arm 5's copy must NOT be copy-pasted from arm 1.** The all-UNKNOWN storm was TRANSIENT — a live poll broke on
poll 1 with `open=36 UNKNOWN=0`, almost certainly GitHub invalidating mergeability behind the five merges. **An
exit-5 red SELF-CLEARS on the next 30-minute run**, which is precisely the property arm 1 laments it lacks ("it
will keep failing every 30 minutes"). Arm 5 says the next run re-reads, and that a PERSISTENT 5 means the read
is genuinely broken. The watch is not a required context, so its red costs an alarm, not a merge. A
wrong-but-red alarm still passes every assertion, so this copy is the one thing no test can catch.

**A harness portability bug in the same file, independently reproduced by DECIDE.** `:239-243` guards on
`command -v git` and on file existence but never on BEING IN A REPO, so `git -C <archive> status` exits 128 and
the harness reports "this slice modified the CONTENDED main-gate-watch.yml". Measured both ways: **52 passed / 1
failed inside a `git archive` extraction, 53 passed / 0 failed in a real checkout.** CI checks out, so CI is
unaffected; every human and agent told to verify from an archive gets a lie. One-line `rev-parse --git-dir`
guard, with an explicit ok/skip line so the absence is STATED rather than assumed.

**Two things deliberately NOT in this slice.** (1) The poll budget — `ATTEMPTS=3`, `SLEEPS="8 20 0"`, ~28s of
waiting, unknown decayed only 41→40→39 — is the proximate cause, but raising it is a tuning guess and **exit 5
makes its inadequacy VISIBLE rather than silent**. Filed. (2) The count+trend: nothing persists a prior run
(no `actions: read`, no artifact, no cache; both cited precedents `absent-context-census.yml:76` and
`crown-reconcile.yml:81` DO carry `actions: read`), and **26% of the watch's runs conclude `cancelled`** — a
third outcome that is neither red nor green, clustered in the 11:34:38–11:34:58 merge burst. A merge burst is
precisely when staleness changes and precisely when the watch goes quiet, so any trend must count a
cancellation as UNREAD, never as unchanged. Filed with that constraint written in.

**Leg 3's green is unreachable this wave and the slice is scoped accordingly.** The population re-derives at
print time to `36 open · 25 CONFLICTING · 11 MERGEABLE · 0 UNKNOWN → RED — 23 reported`; draining the epic's own
four leaves 19 rows, eleven belonging to other epics' charters. **This slice makes the watch's GREEN
trustworthy independently of whether its RED can clear — which is the half that actually deceives.**

### D503 — THE SEAL RUNNER FALSELY REFUSES A PERFECT TREE, AND ITS MUTATION TEST STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE IT.

`seal-predicate.mjs:1151` produces the token's `head=` from `git rev-parse --short HEAD` — ABBREVIATED.
`seal-run.sh:262` compares it with `!=` against the 40-char `ORIGIN_SHA`. The two can never be equal on the live
path, and `--ladder-only` always prints `head=`, so **refusal 5 fires UNCONDITIONALLY** on a full-history,
non-shallow tree parked exactly at origin/main:

```
[exit 5] the token says head=c2de1e51c, which is not origin/main's tip
         c2de1e51cd029d3f47717eec6c53a81b55970364 — the reading describes some other tree.
  do this: take the reading from a worktree parked at origin/main
```

— the state the operator is already in. The pre-run leg (`:218`) is correct (full-to-full); the bug is
exclusively the post-run token leg.

**What it was hiding: nothing bad.** Fixed, the same tree reads `b-rungs=rung1:2,rung2:4,rung3:0 b-clean=6/6
b-unavailable=0/6` and `VOUCHED — SEAL`. The sanctioned instrument has been WITHHOLDING a clean clause-(b)
reading from every operator with a perfect checkout, for its entire life. **"It shadows refusal 6 entirely" is
half right**: refusals are COLLECTED, not short-circuited (`:126-136`), so refusal 6's DIAGNOSIS always printed
— what was shadowed is the EXIT CODE, because `REFUSAL_CODE` takes the FIRST refusal. Proven both ways: unfixed
a tree with `b-unavailable=6/6` exits 5, fixed it exits 6. **Any caller branching on exit 6 has never once seen
it.**

**The harness is blind three ways, not one.** (1) `seal-run.test.sh:170,269` mutate with a 40-char `FAKE_HEAD`,
so a prefix fix still refuses it. (2) The stand-in predicate emits `git rev-parse HEAD` — FULL length —
contradicting the real emitter's `--short` contract, which is why the happy path is green in fixture and red in
life. (3) The "bound to the real emitter" section (`:293-330`) is **GREP-ONLY**: it asserts the field NAME
exists in the source and never executes the real predicate through the runner nor compares the field's SHAPE.
That is the assertion that should have caught this and structurally cannot.

**RULING on the fix, because the obvious one is wrong.** A bare 7-char floor with a plain prefix test STILL
false-refuses a checkout configured `core.abbrev=4` (reproduced: `head=c2de` → exit 5). **Accept the repo's OWN
`git rev-parse --short "$ORIGIN_SHA"` at any length; ELSE require `>= 7` chars AND a genuine prefix.** A floor
of 9 — tempting because this repo abbreviates to 9 — would be worse: git's fixture repos abbreviate to 7 and the
harness's own fixture emitted a 7-char head. After the fix a truthful `--short` head, an explicit 9-char head
and a `core.abbrev=4` head all VOUCH, while a 1-char head, the shipped 40-char lie and a 9-char lie all still
REFUSE.

**Nothing in the repo runs `seal-run.sh`** — `grep -rln seal-run` returns only the two charters plus the script
and its test. No CI green was ever protecting this, and the failure mode is purely human/agent-facing, which is
the worst place for it: this is the instrument D488 built so a wave would stop quoting a reading from the wrong
tree. **`dr-w28-s7`'s criterion 1 is stamped met quoting `token head=<sha> b-unavailable=0/0` — a FIXTURE
reading from the full-length stub; the slice's own vouched-path proof never executed the real predicate.**
Convert the grep-binding into one real end-to-end execution in the same PR, or the next `head=` contract drift
repeats this exactly.

### D504 — ABANDONMENT KEYS ARE DISTINCT, AND THE SEVEN NULL ROWS ARE NEVER BACKFILLED.

Confirmed by running it: a post-#11209 abandoned row (status `failed`, the REAL `abandonment_reason/3`
sentence, all three columns set) loses **all three** keys from `bp cloud site status -o json` while
`failure_class: ABANDONED_AT_CAPACITY` survives. `cloud_site_cmd.go:2264`'s `if siteDeployDeferred(d.Status)`
is the sole cause and `TestSiteDeferralChainNotOnFailedRows` the sole guard (mutation: relax the gate → exactly
that one test reds, package otherwise green). The MACHINE surface is strictly worse than the human one: the
table render still shows "refused 12 rebuilds in a row" in prose while `-o json` carries no numeric key at all.

**Three corrections.** (1) The suppression is a NO-OP today — 0 of 18,642 `failed` rows carry `deferral_depth`;
1,332 of 3,144 `deferred` rows do. **#11209 is what CREATES the drop.** (2) The pinning test's stated rationale
is FALSE: its comment says "a failed row whose reason happens to quote a chain (*the terminal round does*)". It
does not. `refusal N of M in this site's current chain` is written ONLY on the deferred branch
(`deploy.ex:1302`); the abandonment sentence is `… refused N rebuilds in a row for this site, <verdict>`
(`:1424`). **0 of 7 live abandonment rows match `refusal N of M`** — the fixture is a sentence no producer
emits. (3) The drop is not imminent: the fence has NEVER fired in the column era (columns first stamped
2026-08-07 10:12:35Z, last abandonment 03:41:33Z — 6h31m EARLIER; live max depth 9 against bound 12), so
ordering has slack. But the row #11209 finally writes is **the epic's first-ever live abandonment reading**, and
the JSON surface would drop it on arrival.

**RULING: ship `abandonment_depth` / `abandonment_bound` / `abandonment_cause`, gated on the `ABANDONED_*`
class. Do NOT relax `siteDeployDeferred` and do NOT reuse the deferral key names.** Four warrants, each
sufficient. **D195 forbids the alias by name** — "any abandonment reader keys on the anchored abandonment clause
or on `DeployLedger`'s `ABANDONED_*` class — **NEVER on `deferral_depth >= 12`**, which returns zero forever" —
and reusing the names is precisely what would make `deferral_depth >= 12` start working: right for the wrong
reason, and wrong on the busy cause whose bound is 6. Relaxing the gate costs DELETING a guard so data can flow,
which is the failure mode this epic exists to refuse; adding a key costs none. The two facts are semantically
OPPOSITE — on a deferred row depth means "refused N times, RE-QUEUED"; on an abandoned row "refused N times, WE
STOPPED" — so a dashboard summing one key would count a given-up chain as a waiting one, which is the test's
CORRECT worry even though its fixture is fictional. And D221's substring bans (`rate`, `percent`,
`deferral_depth`) are all clear. **Name it `abandonment_*`, not `abandoned_at_*`**: the latter shadows a
timestamp shape in an envelope already carrying `inserted_at` / `became_live_at`, and any consumer
prefix-matching `*_at` mis-types it.

**The reader is COLUMN-FIRST, PROSE-FALLBACK**, exactly as D221 already ruled for the deferral chain: depth from
the column, else from the anchored `refused (\d+) rebuilds in a row` clause; cause from `failure_class`; **bound
COLUMN-ONLY** — the bound is not in the prose, and re-deriving 12/6 in Go would hardcode the other cause's
budget, the mistake D195 names. The asymmetry (depth+cause present, bound absent) **IS** the coverage signal,
honestly rendered. Live-verified: the anchored clause yields 12×6 and 6×1 — D195's exact split — and appears on
**ZERO** non-failed rows, so it is an exclusive predicate.

**RULING: NO BACKFILL — and this is a CHOICE, not an impossibility, which is why it is written down.** The prose
yields depth for all seven. But (a) `dr-w28-rv-abandonment-predicate-replaces-the-prose-regex` (#11202)
criterion 1 demands "the fallback proved reachable", and **these seven are the only live population that can
prove it** — backfilling deletes the evidence the task needs; (b) a synthesised 12 is indistinguishable from a
stamped 12, so `count(deferral_depth) where status='failed'` would read 7 forever and **#11209's first genuine
firing would be unprovable**, a direct violation of D479; (c) `router.ex:11480-11484` already says it — "That
nil is the TRUTHFUL answer and is never coerced to 0" — and a pre-instrument row carrying a post-hoc value is
the same lie one level up; (d) every reader D195 permits already works on all seven today. **Close #11202's
criterion 2 with this D.** Its criterion 1's fallback must also carry a cross-language fixture pinning the Go
regex to the Elixir producer, or a reword breaks it silently in the language the producer-side test cannot see.

**A third silent drop, same file, already live and free to fix here:** `deferral_cause` is decoded
(`client.go:1639`) and referenced in `internal/cli` **only inside a test file** — `siteDeploymentMap` never
emits it, on deferred rows either. That is `deferral_wait`'s "decode is not readership" disease (D453) on a
column that has been on the wire since #10248 and is populated on 1,332 live rows.

**Do NOT make `classify/1` column-first in the same PR** — `dr-w13-bl-column-first-classify-bypass` (#10288):
`consecutive_deferrals/2` synthesises a bare map with no `:deferral_cause`, so a column-first classifier becomes
a second divergent reader.

### D505 — GYLDENDAL: THE RULING SURVIVES, ITS MECHANISM IS REFUTED, AND THE TRANSACTION IS A LEAD ACT.

**Forty-one days live and still worsening.** Re-derived 12:07:43Z: `unreachable` 458 rows ending exactly
07:22:01, `unauthorized` **19 rows** starting 07:37:01 and still arriving (max 12:07:00, ~40s before the read)
— every 15-minute tick, no gap. Row `b1259514` is team **yo**; `gyldendal.barkpark.cloud` is held as
`custom_host` by row `f5e1392e`, team **Gyldendal** — a genuinely different tenant — and `dig` still resolves it
to `116.203.98.0`, Gyldendal's box, which answers 302 while yo's own host answers 308. **Misdelivery 100%**,
`last_seen_at` NULL: the squatting row has never been reached. #10944 is `OPEN/CONFLICTING/DIRTY`, its only
`url` write is a TEST fixture, and **it cannot undo a NULL.**

**D492's MECHANISM IS WRONG and must be amended, not merely superseded, or the refuted premise propagates.**
D492 says `:not_live` "is not a member of `@unavailable_reasons`, so the post-fix envelope falls through to
`unknown` at `:257`". **That chain does not exist.** Three `with/else` clauses (`usage.ex:746`, `:773`, `:785`)
collapse EVERY error — including `{:error, :not_live}` and `{:error, :no_admin_token}` — to the bare atom
`:unmetered`, and `instance_meter(:unmetered, source)` (`:239`) builds a meter with **no `unavailable_reason`
key at all**, never touching `unavailable_reason/1`. Pinned by a test already GREEN on main
(`usage_test.exs:337-343`: `refute Map.has_key?(m.documents, :unavailable_reason)`) and visible in live data
(886 gyldendal rows carry exactly that reasonless shape). **So "does the sampler still write `unknown`?"
answers NO — zero ticks, forever, by construction, and any criterion with an `unknown` denominator MISSES
structurally.** Note also that `:no_admin_token` fires FIRST under the ordered transaction, and D492 named only
`:not_live`.

**D492's RULING survives on a BROADER base than it argued.** The criterion is the DELIVERY-PROVING form — "no
new row carries `unreachable|unauthorized|refused|instance_error`" — and post-fix the meter carries no reason
key whatsoever, so it trivially carries none.
`dr-w28-bl-gyldendal-corrected-criterion-still-unsatisfiable` (open, 0/5) is upgraded from "still PROBABLY
unsatisfiable" to **PROVEN SATISFIABLE**. But its criterion 2 ("verified EMPIRICALLY against a post-fix
envelope") is **unsatisfiable BEFORE the transaction** — no live row has a NULL token (all 8 sampled rows
`tok_null=f`), so production offers no proxy and the post-fix code path has never executed anywhere. It is
verifiable statically plus by the merged test, and that must be written into the criterion. The full criterion
also carries its denominator: **zero delivery-proving reasons across at least 3 consecutive sampler ticks
(≥45 min), with the total new rows in that window printed beside the zero** — a bare zero would also be
produced by the sampler dying, which is the silence this epic exists to catch.

**Ordering CONFIRMED on live data, not reasoned.** Rows with `url='https://gyldendal.barkpark.cloud'` excluding
b1259514 = **0**, so nulling `url` FIRST empties `provisioning_fqdn_claim/1`'s only filter
(`registry.ex:5507`) and returns `:free` with no leg evaluated — `:admin_credential` disarmed by erasure of its
own input. **NULL the token FIRST, url SECOND, one BEGIN/COMMIT**, each `UPDATE` carrying its own guard
predicate so a concurrent write reports `UPDATE 0` instead of clobbering, and the `count(*)=0` re-run INSIDE the
transaction. Both columns are NULLable, so no constraint can fail. Then **rotate team `71069eaa`'s instance
admin token — treat it as disclosed to team `9d71ba21`'s box.**

**WHY IT IS NOT A SLICE, stated in writing as leg 4 requires.** It is a production credential write against
another tenant's row, lead-ordered by construction; no builder may run it. **And the remediated state is
provable only as an ABSENCE** — after the transaction the meters revert to a byte-shape identical to the
pre-08-04 blind era, so a silent regression (token or url restored by any future provisioning path) reports
NOTHING. That is this epic's founding sin re-created by its own fix. The remedy — admit `:not_live` /
`:no_admin_token` to `@unavailable_reasons` (`usage.ex:161-162`) and pass the typed reason through the `else`
clauses instead of flattening to `:unmetered` — turns the remediated state into a POSITIVE, monitorable
reading. **It is NOT built this wave because `usage.ex`'s credential-egress path is CCH's fence and this edit
sits on it.** Filed with the fence question named, for a CCH ruling first.

Trap for the next agent: `grep -rn unavailable_reason cloud/test/` in the PRIMARY checkout returns **0** while

### D511 — THE CROWN'S rc=2 IS A DEFERRAL WITH NO RE-READ, AND IT SWALLOWED A REAL RED TODAY.

The direction said run 31316266634 "exits rc=0". **REFUTED — it exited rc=2** via the serving-grace arm
(`crown-reconcile.sh:565`, `SERVING_GRACE_SECONDS=1200`), and `crown-reconcile.yml:123` maps rc=2 to `exit 0`
under text that itself reads *"That is a SILENCE, not a green."* The run is reported **success**.

Also refuted: "every push run is condemned to rc=2." Three push runs the same minute — 31316057500, 31316075489,
31316124609 — printed `RECONCILED: all 3 delivering run(s) …` and exited 0. The grace is cadence-dependent.

**The defect neither premise named, and it is the sharpest thing this wave found.** PR #11255's merge commit
`4c8314c94` had its deploy run 31316124617 **CANCELLED with ZERO jobs**, so no row could ever be written — yet
barkpark.cloud SERVED it from ~13:34Z to 13:42Z. That is textbook SERVING-UNRECORDED, the exact sentence
`crown-reconcile.sh:610` exists to print. Four consecutive runs SAW it (ages **-3s / 53s / 105s / 200s**) and
each downgraded it to a warning. At 13:42:23Z the box moved to 02475d0ec, and the serving check only ever reads
the CURRENT serving sha. **There is no queue, no re-ask list, no persisted "come back to this sha" — so the
accusation is now permanently unmakeable.** The instrument detected the epic's founding failure mode on live
production four times in four minutes and reported it zero times.

Compounding it: the exit-2 message at `:633` prints exactly three counters (BEHIND_UNREADABLE, JOBS_UNREADABLE,
UNCLASSIFIED) while `UNREADABLE=1` is set at **eight** distinct sites, five of which no counter tracks. All four
graced runs printed `COULD NOT FULLY READ: 0 sha(s) unreadable, 0 run(s) with no job list, 0 row(s) with carried
never measured` — **all zeros, while exiting 2**. And `age=$((NOW - since))` is unguarded: run 31316144030
printed "only **-3s** old" and treated a clock skew as leniency. **RULED: the grace must ARM A RE-READ, the
exit-2 message must NAME the cause that fired, and `age < 0` is a fault, not leniency.** This is unruled ground
— D500–D509 say nothing about the serving grace.

### D512 — THE 401 IS BY DESIGN AND ALREADY RULED. THE FIX IS A CREDENTIAL, NOT A DOOR.

`router.ex:3917` is `require_user_or_pat([]) |> require_ability("read")`, and the router's own table line 107
says *"PAT-reachable on purpose (D385/D412)"*. **D437 measured this before the reconciler ever ran.** WORKER_TOKEN
is a faceless principal that authenticates nowhere, so it halts 401 BEFORE `require_ability` — which is why the
code is 401 and never 403.

**The PAT path now has its first end-to-end execution in the epic's life.** A real minted read-ability PAT
(`dr-w30-verifier-probe`, minted and revoked in-run, 401 after revoke, no residue) drives `crown-reconcile.sh`'s
`:311` branch to `reader=pat`, **exit 0, `RECONCILED: all 5 delivering run(s) … all 54 row(s) …`, with ZERO
"answered HTTP" warnings**. So the arm works; it is unselectable in CI for one structural reason:
`crown-reconcile.yml`'s reconcile step env is GH_TOKEN + CP_HOST + DEPLOY_SSH_KEY only, and **`gh secret list`
returns exactly six secrets, none named CROWN_API_TOKEN**. The secret does not exist.

**RULED, and it splits across the human/build line.** (a) HUMAN GATE — the lead mints a read-ability PAT and
stores it as repository secret `CROWN_API_TOKEN`; no builder can do this. (b) BUILD — one env line, plus the
reconciler stating `read_via:` as a first-class verdict field instead of burying five 401s in `note:`. Widening
the route is **FILED, NOT BUILT**: it lives inside cloud-console-hardening's bare-`cloud/` fence (D94), and
`dr-w24-bl-internal-write-route-is-publicly-reachable` already argues against concentrating that secret further.

**Blast radius correction: "every non-SSH reader is DARK" is FALSE.** The console reads
`/v1/notifications/deliveries` and `/v1/operator/deliveries` — a different table; `digest_email.ex`,
`daily_digest_worker.ex` and `deploy_ledger.ex` carry ZERO references to the platform delivery record. The 401's
blast radius is ONE consumer: crown-reconcile's CI read path.

### D513 — rc=2 IS OVERLOADED THREE WAYS, AND THE WATCH HAS NEVER PRODUCED A MEANINGFUL GREEN.

`stale-verdict-watch.sh` returns 2 from three conditions of two kinds: **(A)** the PR list was never read at all
(`:158`, propagated `:315`) — zero coverage, and rate-limit/abuse are deliberately routed here; **(B)** main's
commit history was never read (`:324`) — population known, staleness distance unknowable; **(C)** rows still
UNKNOWN after re-polling (`:367`) — the genuine warning. Only C is what the message says. Both silences
reproduce hermetically with nothing but `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`.

**RULED: add 6 = UNREACHABLE and 7 = DISTANCE UNREADABLE.** Two codes, not one — different remedies (token/poll
budget vs the commits API), different residual knowledge, and a 7 could later be downgraded to a partial verdict
while a 6 never can. Reusing 3 is REFUSED for the reason the file's own header already gives: for one release 3
and 4 were the same code and "the size fault wore the credential fault's name." Arms **0, 1, 3, 4, 5 stay
byte-identical**; arm 2's text loses its now-false "or the pull-request list could not be read" clause.
Fail-open warning that must survive into the build: B's early return is load-bearing — falling through with an
empty commits array makes `commits_since` return 0 for every green and `select(.since >= 1)` drops all of them,
**manufacturing a clean verdict**.

**And the worse finding.** Run **31316075524** (push, 13:32:37Z) concluded **SUCCESS** having classified **ZERO
of 42 open rows** — every row `mergeable=UNKNOWN`, the rc=2 arm taken, green reported on a population of zero.
The other greens are a DIFFERENT JOB: `stale-verdict-harness` runs on `pull_request` while the watch itself is
skipped there. **So the watch has never once produced a green that means "no PR is asserting a stale verdict."**
The arm-5 BLIND fix (#11256, 899aa34c0, merged 13:34:10Z) landed **93 seconds after** that blind green, so its
own comment claiming 31311358759 is "the ONLY push run that ever concluded success" is already false on main.

### D514 — THE WATCH'S GREEN IS UNREACHABLE INSIDE THIS EPIC'S FENCE, AND THE CHARTER'S OWN NUMBER WAS WRONG.

Run live from origin/main: `35 open · 25 CONFLICTING · 10 MERGEABLE · 0 UNKNOWN` → **RED, 23 CONFLICTING**.

Draining the four the direction names leaves **19** — which reproduces D502's number exactly. But D502's
*"eleven belonging to other epics' charters"* is **WRONG: only 9 of the 19 are foreign, and only 4 of those are
other-epic charter PRs. Ten of the 19 are this epic's own.** The drain we can scope is roughly twice what the
charter believed. **Draining all 14 of ours still leaves 9. No act inside this fence reaches green** — a slice
promising green would be dishonest, and D502 already conceded this.

**A TRAP IN THAT DRAIN, and it is destructive if missed.** Four of our ten (#10173, #10407, #10496, #10522) are
this epic's own stranded wave charters. `grep -cE '^#+ +(D25[0-9]|D3[0-2][0-9]) '` over origin/main's charter

### D521 — PUSHDELIVERYWORKER: LEAVE THE OPTION ALONE. COPYING #11255 HERE WOULD BE THE REGRESSION.

anywhere can distinguish the two configurations.** The existing replay test replays while the first job is still
`:available`, a state both configurations dedupe; only `:completed` separates them and nothing reaches it.

Writing the missing behavioural test settles it: on main's config it **PASSES**; under the mutation it **FAILS**
`left: {:ok, 0}` / `right: {:ok, 1}`. **So main is correct and the "fix" is the regression** — an instance's
at-least-once redelivery arriving after the first push landed would send the user a SECOND identical push. The
worker is event-driven and its uniqueness key is the full args, whose `blocked_since` is the event's identity,
so two byte-identical payloads inside 600s can only be a replay. One producer, one call site
(`push.ex:220` ← `router.ex:7790`). **RULED: keep `:completed` in the window; add the behavioural PIN so the
next reader cannot "tidy" it away.** The residue task's FILES list names
`cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/workers/push_delivery_worker_test.exs`, **a path that does not exist** — the real
files are under `cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/push/`.

**WHAT LANDED.** The wave's centre of gravity is s1, and it is the most consequential instrument fix the epic
has made. `crown-reconcile.sh` granted a serving grace and persisted NOTHING while only ever reading the sha
the box serves right now, so any sha replaced inside 1200s was structurally unaccusable — which is how
`4c8314c94` was graced four times in four minutes and then vanished. A granted grace now writes
`<sha> <first-seen-epoch>` to a RE-ASK LIST that outlives the run, and every later run re-asks the CROWN, not
the box. `UNREADABLE=1` collapsed from nine scattered sites to one (`reason()`), so the exit-2 sentence
enumerates the conditions that actually fired instead of printing three counters that read all zeros on every
graced run. `age < 0` stopped meaning "be lenient". s2 split the watch's overloaded rc=2 into 6 UNREACHABLE and
7 DISTANCE UNREADABLE, each exiting 1 with its own remedy, with arms 0/1/3/4/5 byte-identical. s4 found

by DERIVING the expectations from the ratchets rather than re-pinning numbers, and only then wired 13
uninvoked harnesses into `shell-harnesses.yml` with 33 explicit per-file paths mirrored on `pull_request` and
`push:[main]`. s5 turned a refused census share from a dead-end em-dash into the `--from` that would answer it
— read from the plane's own refusal envelope, never hardcoded — and the suggested window un-refuses all
fourteen classes live. s3 is one word (`box_exploded` → `runner_start_failed`) that unblocks #11209 without
seating a fabricated cause word in the taxonomy. s6 pinned a claim, not a bug: D521 ruled main's config CORRECT
and this wave wrote the only test that reaches `:completed`, so the next reader cannot tidy it away.

**REVIEWER FIXES, in place.** Two, both small and both pinned. On s4: `timeout-minutes: 15` on all thirteen
`shell-harnesses.yml` jobs — GitHub's default is 360 minutes, so a hang in a harness that finishes in seconds
would have held a runner for six hours, the same class of silence this lane exists to end. On s5:
`deployCensusShareNotes` grouped refused rows by REASON alone, and the plane's straddle reason carries no
denominator, so two rows sharing a reason but denominated over different samples printed one row's `n` beside a

## WAVE 31 — 2026-08-09 — CURE THE RANKING, AND DISCOVER THE RANKING IS A PHOTOGRAPH OF A DEAD HOUR

**THE WAVE'S PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE ITS OWN VERIFICATION, AND THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING NINETEEN
SURVEY REPORTS AND EIGHT VERIFIERS PRODUCED.** Wave 31 was convened to cure the top of D516's ranking on four
arms. Three of those four arms are aimed at classes with **zero live rows**. The founding number has already
moved, for reasons that predate this wave, and the honest deliverable is naming that — with the arithmetic —
rather than reaching for an AFTER the window cannot supply.

### D524 — EVERY CLASS D516 RANKS IS DEAD. THE RANKING IS TRUE AND IT IS A PHOTOGRAPH OF A SIX-HOUR INCIDENT.

Re-derived by running against cloud-db-1 (sanity total 32,855 rows all-time, 2026-07-14 → 2026-08-09; failed
18,643 / live 10,943 / deferred 3,269 — no query returned a vacuous zero). Last-fired, by class:
`BOX_500` **2026-08-06 03:16:37** (301 rows, one ~6h cascade; zero rows in the remaining 3.5 days of D516's
own window). `BOX_DEPLOY_DISABLED_503` **2026-08-07 03:19:21** (219 in-window, 265 all-time, zero since).
`BOX_BUSY_DEFERRED` **2026-08-07 08:16:29**. `BUILD_FAILED` **2026-08-06 22:20:47**. The entire live failure
population since 2026-08-08 is **21 rows in 40 hours** fleet-wide: `BOX_UNREACHABLE` 8, `DOC_ID_EMPTY` 8,
`PROCESS_DIED` 3+1, `BOX_RATE_LIMITED_429` 1. **D516 ranks these classes #1/#2/#3 only because its window's
left edge opens ~2 minutes before a host incident.** The ranking is not wrong; it is retrospective. RULING:
a cause ranking must carry a **last-fired instant per class** beside its share, or it will keep nominating

### D525 — DEFERRALS SETTLE, 3,217 OF 3,217. THE COLLAPSE IS A REAL CURE, NOT A RELABEL — AND THE HEADLINE RATE IS DILUTED 2.2×.

fired. **Therefore the 86.76% → 0.41% collapse is REAL:** on a denominator that excludes deferrals entirely
(`failed/(failed+live)`), the rate still falls **87.19% (08-01) → 60.47% (08-06) → 3.14% (08-07) → 1.36%

### D529 — THE LEAK GUARD ARM B RELIES ON IS CURRENTLY DEAD CODE, AND SHIPPING THE RELAXATION ALONE MAKES IT PERMANENTLY UNPROVABLE.

`error_render_integration_test.exs:29` asserts `message == "unknown error"` strictly; the leak guard
`refute message =~ "boom"` is at **:30, not :31** (:31 is `refute Map.has_key?(decoded, "errors")`). Under an
`Exception.message/1` mutation ExUnit aborts at :29 and **:30 NEVER RUNS** — the guard cannot lose. Only after
relaxing :29 to a shape admitting the family suffix did :30 finally red (`left: "unknown error (boom — …)"`),
and the family-only implementation then passed 33/0. **RULING: the relaxation of :29 and the retention of :30
are ONE acceptance criterion, discharged by a pasted `Exception.message/1` mutation that REDS :30. Shipping
the relaxation without that proof is a guard with a shebang.** Two further constraints: `error_json_test.exs:23`
renders with an EMPTY assigns map, so the implementation MUST keep a nil-reason fallback to `{:error, :unknown}`;
and `:exit`/`:throw` deliver a BARE TERM as `assigns.reason` (`Exception.normalize/3` structifies only `:error`,
turning even `:badarg` into `ArgumentError`), so the implementation MUST branch on `assigns.kind` — a
`reason.__struct__` raise inside the error renderer costs the client its response entirely. A
`Plug.Conn.WrapperError` never reaches the view (`render_errors.ex:41-43` destructures it first), so **no
unwrap step may be added**.

### D533 — THE SCOREBOARD, COMMITTED BEFORE THE FIRST LINE OF BUILD CODE, WITH ITS REFUSAL CONDITIONS PRE-DECLARED.

`failure_rate` cannot distinguish a cure from a relocation: 219 rows moving failed→live and 219 moving
failed→deferred both give **14.06%, byte-identical**. `fr_settled` separates them (**30.91% vs 33.67%**) and is
D3-legal (a rate, pinned window, volume printed). PRIMARY = `fr_settled` **reported only beside the full
partition**; `fr_all` secondary, never quoted alone; an absolute `live` count beside both, because `live` is
read positively off `status == "live"` and cannot be moved by a taxonomy or message change. Clocks, re-measured
on a quiet read: fleet volume 40.92 rows/h → n=200 in **4.89h**; settled failures 0.52/h → **≈16 days**;
`DOC_ID_EMPTY` 0.203/h → **≈41 days** — and arrivals are BURSTY (CV 1.100, 30 zero-attempt hours in 168), so a
mean-based ETA is a fiction. **Three refusal conditions, declared now:** INSUFFICIENT VOLUME (<200 in the
affected cohort → publish the raw partition, no percentage — **pre-declared TRUE for every class-level claim
this wave**); DENOMINATOR SHRINK (AFTER volume <60% of BEFORE at equal wall-clock → comparison VOID regardless
of the rate); INHERITED CURE (D526). A BEFORE with an open right edge is a moving target dressed as a
measurement — two runs three minutes apart returned `fr_settled` 4.38 then 4.37 on **zero new failures** — so
every BEFORE carries `observed_through` and closes its right edge at the first builder's merge instant. The
AFTER query is pinned as a FILE at `tooling/grip/ledger/deploy-reliability-w31-after-2026-08-09.sql`
(runs rc=0, non-vacuous: rewound to the D516 boundary it reproduces 5,965/1,045 and flips all four verdicts to
SUFFICIENT; at now it prints INSUFFICIENT VOLUME on all four). One correction it carries:
`count(DISTINCT failure_reason)` over the 500 family is a FALSE cure signal because BUILD_FAILED reasons embed
the build clock (10 rows → 10 "distinct"); the honest metric is **top_string_share per subfamily**.

## WAVE 32 — 2026-08-09 — THE FLEET GENUINELY GOT WELL, THE HEADLINE IS UNAUDITABLE, AND THE EPIC NAMES ITS EXIT

Wave 31 asked the best question this epic has ever asked and could not answer it: the failure rate collapsed
86.76% → 0.41% exactly as `deferred` appeared as a status, so either the fleet got well or 1,045 failures were
relabelled as 3,217 deferrals. Wave 32 settled it against the live control-plane database, with two independent
keys and a served-state corroboration, and then discovered that the verdict — while true — rests on arithmetic
no shipped instrument can reproduce. This wave publishes the settlement, cures the four defects that have a live
population, reclaims a ledger that overstates its own remaining work by roughly a third, and answers the owner's
third question in plain words: **WIND DOWN to a maintenance cadence.**

- **D537 — JOB ONE IS SETTLED: THE FLEET GENUINELY GOT WELL. IT IS A CURE, NOT AN ACCOUNTING ARTEFACT.**
  Sanity total first, so nothing below is a vacuous zero: 32,953 rows, 2026-07-14 11:28:18 → 2026-08-09 18:01:41,
  failed 18,652 / live 10,974 / deferred 3,327. On the CHARTER-SANCTIONED time-keyed classifier
  (`deferral_outcome/3`, `deploy_ledger.ex:1396`: `content_rev = ''` → UNREADABLE; else the FIRST later `live`
  row on the same `{site_id, environment}` → COVERED; else PENDING), trailing 72h reads **COVERED 2,718
  (99.7797%) / PENDING 6 (0.2203%) / UNREADABLE 0**, and all six PENDING are 1.5–2.6 minutes old carrying the
  same in-flight `content_rev`. Re-run with a 60-minute settle cutoff: **2,701 settled deferrals, 0 PENDING,
  0 UNREADABLE — 100.0000% COVERED.** All-time on rows older than 24h: deferred **0 never-covered of 2,816**;
  failed **5 never-covered of 18,640**, and 2 of those 5 are the only two `environment='preview'` rows in the
  entire table, so **production never-covered, all-time, is 3** — independently reproducing
  `settle-cutoff-sensitivity`'s "3 lost all-time", both on sites that never served a build in their history.
  Corroborated off served state, which no taxonomy change can move: per-site staleness over 14d is 0.02–1.36h on
  the six sites that have deferrals; the four stale sites (20h–248h) have zero pending work.
  **The collapse is real.** D525's verdict stands, on a better key than D525 used.

- **D538 — THE `(site_id, content_rev)` CHAIN KEY IS DECLINED FOR THE FOURTH TIME, AND THE SANCTIONED KEY
  REPRODUCES THE SAME VERDICT WITH ZERO RESIDUE, SO NOTHING IS OWED TO IT.** Strategize proposed ratifying the
  chain `(site_id, content_rev)` as "the epic's unit of truth" on a measured 34.09% never-live rate with a
  100.00% supersession discriminator. D162 rules `content_rev` is not a revision (a `sha256([doc_type,
  published_count, published_events])` over a dataset-wide activity window; 90.72% of revved rows carry a rev
  that appears on more than one site; 282 `(site, rev)` groups RECUR after another rev intervened, holding 28.7%
  of revved rows); D170(a) lists a revision-keyed census under DECLINED-OUT-LOUD; D478 declines it AGAIN one wave
  ago and strikes the word **superseded** by name because it "names an inference the row cannot support."
  **THE DECIDING CROSS-TAB:** the declined key's 504 never-live chains classify on the sanctioned key as
  `deferred|COVERED 471 + failed|COVERED 33 = 504`, **PENDING 0** — every chain the declined key called
  superseded, the sanctioned key calls COVERED, same population, no row between them. Strategize's 34.09% IS the
  52.1% manufactured loss D162 predicted, and its 100.00% discriminator IS the correction. **RULED: the chain key
  is not ratified, the word `superseded` does not ship, and the epic's published unit stays the
  sanctioned time-keyed COVERED partition.** Its permitted wording is D478's, unchanged: *the site has since
  rebuilt*, never *your edit shipped*.

- **D539 — THE HEADLINE IS TRUE AND UNAUDITABLE, AND THAT — NOT RELIABILITY — IS THE RESIDUAL GAP.** The ledger
  has no field distinguishing an absorbed deferral from a dropped one; 0.39% would read byte-identically on a
  fleet that had silently lost 468 publishes. The settlement above was computed BY HAND against the production
  database. Closing that is this wave's instrument work, and it is a REPAIR of a live instrument, not a new
  front: `deferral_wait` already ships COVERED/PENDING/UNREADABLE with p50/p95/max, is already aggregated in
  `census/3`, and is already read by `internal/cli/cloud_deploy_census_cmd.go:400,1040-1136`. **ONE HONEST
  AMENDMENT:** the classifier's population is `status='deferred'` ONLY (`deploy_ledger.ex:1291`), so a gauge
  built on it alone is blind to the **33 of 504** never-live chains that terminate `failed`. Wave 32 extends the
  same clock to failed-terminating rows and publishes the partition in the DAILY DIGEST, which already runs
  `0 6 * * *` per team (`config.exs:334` → `digest_email.ex:301`) and therefore ships with a human reader by
  construction — the one carrier this epic can wind down onto without inventing a scheduler.

- **D540 — `delivery/3`'s MODULEDOC IS FALSE ON TODAY'S CORPUS, AND THE STALENESS RUNS IN EXACTLY THE DIRECTION
  D537 PREDICTS.** Its load-bearing sentence, verbatim on origin/main, is `ON TODAY'S CORPUS p95 REFUSES AT EVERY
  WIDTH ... 40%+ of rows in any window are still waiting`. Measured by running the function itself against
  cloud-db-1: `censored_fraction` is **0.0139 at 24h, 0.0027 at 72h, 0.0013 at 7d, 0.0004 at 14d** — a 30–100×
  collapse. p95 prints at every width ≥6h (24h **948.782s**, 72h **1256.78s**); only `max` refuses, and it
  refuses structurally (0.0 headroom), not for corpus health. It is reachable on the wire today:
  `bp cloud deployments --days 1` returns `delivery.p95 = {"seconds":948.782,"refused":false}`. **RULED:** the
  instrument that was built to refuse because the fleet was sick now answers because the fleet is well — that is
  independent corroboration of D537, and the moduledoc must be corrected in the same slice that touches the
  clock. **The wave publishes `delivery/3`'s numbers, never Strategize's chain figures (p50 61s / p95 422s):**
  those drop the censored third (n=979 of 1,458), key on a declined key, and their p50 of 61s is numerically
  identical to the charter's measured ENQUEUE LAG p50 and to `@schedule_in_default` — they measure the
  scheduler's floor, not content waiting. **EVERY PUBLISHED PERCENTILE PINS ITS WINDOW AND ITS CLOCK INLINE:**
  p95 moves 948.8s → 211,338s → 540,548s across 24h/7d/14d, a 570× spread on an unchanged fleet.

- **D541 — THE `FunctionClauseError` POPULATION IS LOCATED, THE LEAD'S NUMBER IS EXACT, AND BOTH INHERITED
  DETAILS ABOUT IT WERE WRONG.** Guerrilla serves `barkpark-slot@blue`; `@green` is the dark standby with
  347,694 journal lines and ZERO occurrences — which is why an earlier scan reported the population absent. On
  blue, trailing 24h: **`Sent 500` = 299, `FunctionClauseError` = 33.** Exactly the lead's 33-of-299. All 33
  carry ONE tuple head: `traverse_errors({:invalid_epic_paper_quality, …})`. **The feeder is NOT the `if_rev`
  precondition fence** (a stale-`if_rev` POST returns 409, proved live) — it is the epic-paper-quality wall.
  `AuthoringWall.enforce/5` returns SIX rejection shapes; `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` hand-routes four
  (`label_spine`, `invalid_paper_structure`, `unknown_tag`, `duplicate_of`) and then falls into a **bare
  `{:error, changeset}`** catch-all at lines **209, 278, 337**, handing a 2-tuple to
  `Ecto.Changeset.traverse_errors/2`. `MutateController` has no such bug — it routes everything through
  `Errors.to_envelope/2`, and `errors.ex:481` ALREADY builds the 422 envelope for this exact code. **The cure is
  a `%Ecto.Changeset{}` guard plus a routing tail; no new envelope, no contract change.** Proved red-before by
  mutation (`FunctionClauseError` at `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex:906`) and green-after (47 tests, 0 failures)
  with the locked `invalid_paper` contract test still green. **THE SELF-REFERENTIAL BITE:** this defect 500s the
  epic cycle's OWN wave-Paper publish, and `dr-w30-bl-paper-ingest-limits-500-with-no-detail` — filed at wave 30
  from wave 30's own Paper, "every new heading 500s" past `@max_top_level_headings 16` — IS this defect.

- **D542 — `dedup_unavailable` IS THE SECOND ORPHAN, AND ROUTING IT THROUGH THE SHARED ENVELOPE DESCRIBES AN
  OUTAGE AS A POLICY VETO.** `to_envelope({:error, {:dedup_unavailable, _}})` yields `409 / code "halted" /
  hint "A plugin's lifecycle hook vetoed this write"`. That is a transient E4 outage told to a client as a
  document problem, and 409 invites a fix rather than a retry. **RULED:** the ingest slice routes it explicitly
  and does NOT inherit the `halted` wording; a dedicated arm is required, and the wording change to
  `errors.ex:455` is FILED separately so a wall fix and a contract change do not ride one PR.

- **D543 — THE MAJORITY OUTCOME OF `bp cloud site deploy` IS A TEN-MINUTE LIE, AND IT HAS BEEN FILED SINCE WAVE
  7.** `deferred` is terminal server-side (`registry/deployment.ex:95` → `"deferred" => []`) and absent from
  `cloudclient.SiteDeploymentTerminal` (`client.go:1674`), whose own comment asserts the enum "has SIX values"
  when `@statuses` lists seven. Reproduced end-to-end against the package's own fake control plane, first poll
  `deferred`: **pollHits=300 (the full 300×2s ≈ 10-minute budget), exit=0, stdout `… deploy in progress (stage
  BUILD)`** — and the server's refusal reason on the wire, never printed. `-o json` is identical on polls and
  exit code. `TestSiteDeploymentTerminal` names `deferred` in NEITHER list, so it is structurally blind.
  Deferral is **73.7% of settled attempts** (D209's AFTER window: 1,119 deferred of 1,519). **THE FIX IS NOT ONE
  LINE:** `siteDeployWaiting` (`cloud_site_cmd.go:1887`) is defined as `!SiteDeploymentTerminal(s)` and dr-w12 S7
  deliberately made deferred count as waiting; the naive one-line change reds FOUR tests including
  `TestSiteWaitingSinceMeasuresADeferralChainFromItsStart`. The full candidate fix (~12 lines, 2 files) leaves
  the entire `./internal/...` suite green and collapses 300 polls to 1. **EXIT-CODE RULING: `deferred` KEEPS
  exit 0.** D537 measured coverage at 100.00% — the content reaches the site — so a non-zero exit would turn
  ~74% of deploy invocations red for an outcome that loses nothing, which is the cry-wolf failure this wave is
  trying to prevent, landed on the operator surface instead of the pager. **What is dishonest is the SENTENCE
  and the ten minutes, not the code.** The verdict must name the refusal, its chain position and the re-queue,
  reusing `siteDeferralLine` (`cloud_site_cmd.go:1012`). An opt-in `--wait-for-live` is filed, not built.

- **D544 — THE ABANDONMENT ARM HAS FIRED SEVEN TIMES IN PRODUCTION, D134 UNDERCOUNTS BY THREE, AND ITS OWN
  STRUCTURED MARKER IS A SIXTH ZERO-READING INSTRUMENT.** Never say "the lapse has never fired." Prose scan
  returns **7 rows**: 1× `already_running` at 6 rounds (2026-08-05 22:57:53) and 6× `box_at_capacity` at 12
  rounds (2026-08-07 01:20:14 → 03:41:33) across five sites. The structured predicate
  `deferral_depth = deferral_bound` matches **0 of 32,953 rows** — and not by accident: `defer/3` fires the
  abandonment arm at `prior >= bound - 1` (`deploy.ex:1275`) so the bound-th round is written `failed`, capping
  any `deferred` row at bound−1; **the predicate is UNSATISFIABLE by construction.** Worse, the column writer's
  first stamped row is 2026-08-07 10:12:35.033826 — **6h31m01s after the last abandonment** — so all 7 predate
  their own marker and the ONLY way to find one today is the prose scan wave 28 landed to abolish.
  **Backfill is fully derivable, 7 of 7, 0 underivable** (depth from the sentence's own `refused N rebuilds`,
  cause from the two `terminal_verdict/1` literals, and **bound := derived_depth**, never today's constant).
  **ORDERING IS LAW: the backfill merges BEFORE `dr-w28-rv-abandonment-predicate-replaces-the-prose-regex`.**
  Landing that swap first silently drops every historical abandonment out of the cohort and hands the wind-down
  a permanent zero manufactured by the epic's own cleanup.
  **AND THE RESIDUAL RISK THE WIND-DOWN MUST NAME OUT LOUD:** 2 of the 7 abandoned publishes never reached
  `live` at their own `content_rev` and were saved only by a later build on the same site. The abandonment path
  CAN lose a publish; it is bounded, classified and counted as a failure — but it is not nothing.

- **D545 — WAVE 31's rc=2 → exit 1 ALREADY CRIED WOLF FIVE TIMES OUT OF SIX, AND THE RECONCILER IS CURRENTLY
  100% NOISE AND 100% BLIND AT THE SAME TIME.** rc=2 has fired **six times in the workflow's entire (one-day)
  history and zero times since 6f8a7016** — and the zero is bad news: since that merge the product step
  `Does the crown match what was actually deployed?` is `skipped` in all five runs because the self-test step
  fails first, while `file-ci-failure-issue.sh` commented on #11217 five times in five minutes asserting *"The
  platform's delivery record does not match what was deployed"* — a comparison that never ran. Of the six rc=2
  firings, **5 were the benign in-flight SERVING GRACE** (four of them the same sha graced four times in four
  minutes, one at a **−3s** negative process age) and one was an unnamed pre-#11365 unreadable; **0 were a real
  crown mismatch.** The harness red is environment-dependent, not a regression: `crown-reconcile.test.sh:484`
  builds a NOTOOLS shim but keeps `/usr/bin` on PATH, so on a runner `gh` is `/usr/bin/gh` and is never removed —
  **137/137 locally, 136/137 in CI.** And `/var/lib/crown-reconcile/graced.txt` **does not exist on CP_HOST**
  (the directory holds one 12-byte `probe` file), which `crown-reconcile.sh:405` reports ABSENT → `reason()` →
  `UNREADABLE=1` → exit 2 → page. **RULED, and the order is the whole ruling:** (a) make the harness assertion
  CI-honest so the reconciler can speak at all; (b) tolerate an absent re-ask list on a first run; (c) ONLY then
  split rc=2 so a young in-flight grace WARNS and the ABSENT list and transport silence still PAGE. Ship (a)+(c)
  without (b) and the operator's first-ever delivered crown alarm is a false one about a file that has never
  existed.

- **D546 — THE EPIC'S OWN LEDGER HAS THE IDENTICAL DISCLOSURE DISEASE, AND "N OPEN CHILDREN" IS NOT EVIDENCE OF
  REMAINING WORK.** The GOAL carries 280 children: **199 open** (not 198) / 73 done / 8 cancelled. Partitioned
  with D536's mergeCommit test (this repo squash-merges, so the branch-head test is structurally always wrong):
  **76 LANDED-BUT-OPEN** (a merged `Task:` line whose mergeCommit is an ancestor of origin/main), **6
  DUPLICATE/SHADOW** `drafts.*` rows, **1 ZOMBIE** re-filed under another slug, **116 GENUINELY OPEN**. 76 is a
  FLOOR: D536 names two further rows cured on main whose PRs wrote `Refs:` and prose instead of a `Task:` line,
  so landed ≥78 and genuine ≤114. **52 of the 76 sit at exactly N−1**, because the single unmet criterion is in
  every case the merge-gated one the builder was forbidden to stamp. **The `Task:` line is the ONLY
  machine-readable link between a row and its landing** — where a builder wrote prose, the row is invisible to
  every automated reclaim, which is the deferral-marker defect wearing a different hat. Of the 116 genuinely
  open, **89 sit at 0/N — never started**, and only 18 at N−1: the epic is not a tail of nearly-finished work, it
  is a backlog the last six waves filed faster than they built. **RULED per D520 (measured 0% execution rate for
  judgement-shaped lead acts written as charter prose): the reclaim is FILED AS A TASK, not written here.**
  **AND THE METHOD CORRECTION, because the naive recipe overstates by 35%:** `gh pr list --search <slug>` is
  tokenized and fuzzy (it returns PRs whose bodies never contain the slug), a body that MENTIONS a slug is
  usually saying it is NOT done ("pulled out", "FOLLOW-UP FILED", "NOT DONE HERE"), and it MISSES PRs outright —
  it never returns #11075, the PR that actually landed `dr-w25-s4`. Require a standalone `Task:` line AND scan
  main's own commit messages as a second source.

- **D547 — FOUR INHERITED MERGE PREMISES WERE STALE; #10400 IS SUPERSEDED, NOT PENDING.** #11364 (mergeCommit
  `b03f3d8f`, which IS origin/main's tip at read time) and #11368 (`d9befa36`, its parent) are **MERGED** —
  movement (3)'s "land them" was already done before a builder saw the brief. **#10400 must be CLOSED, not
  rebased:** its head defines 78 tests in `deploy_ledger_test.exs` against main's 93 and `comm -23` of the two
  sorted name sets is EMPTY — zero tests it has that main lacks — while its `deploy_ledger.ex` is **688 lines
  behind** main (the "byte-identical" phrase in the digest describes #11368's rebase branch, not this PR). The
  stranded branch `origin/loop-epic/the-content-api-s-own-status-stops-being-1` is deleted with it. **#10129
  stays PARKED** — D167 and D185 already ruled its rebase semantic, not mechanical (a ten-rung vs eight-rung
  attention ladder), and its real conflict set is SIX files including `client.go` and `semrole.go`; no builder is
  assigned to it. **#10811 is merge-pathed:** its real conflict set is only THREE files and — refuting the
  inherited premise — `internal/cloudclient/client.go` merges CLEAN; it is the only Go reader for
  `coalesced_attempts`, which `git grep` proves absent from `internal/` on main.

- **D548 — THE SOBELOW RED IS A BASELINE LINE-SHIFT ON MAIN ITSELF, NOT A NEW FINDING AND NOT #11364's.** The
  deciding command `mix sobelow --skip --exit Low` prints exactly THREE findings, all
  `Config.CSRF: Missing CSRF Protections` in `router.ex` at pipelines `media_mutate:622`, `user_auth:563`,

  `3af348c9` — **main is red on its own.** Do NOT count the reconcile step's ~100 findings: that step runs after
  the decision and decides nothing (the "read the gate's scan, not the log" rule, recurring for the third time).

- **D549 — THE BOX_UNREACHABLE BURST IS AN INCIDENT, THEREFORE AN ALARM TARGET, NOT A CURE TARGET — AND NINE
  ROWS MOVE THE EPIC HEADLINE 4×.** The 17:00Z burst is 9 rows / 6 sites spanning **00:02:47.86**, all stage
  `PLAN`, all ONE string, with deploys live at 17:36 and again at 17:47 — the box was unreachable for under three
  minutes, never down. Gap-grouped at 30 minutes it is the 58th such episode in 24 days (143 rows, median episode
  **1 row**); every one self-healed. At identical 24h width the headline reads **1.50% / 4.30%** containing the
  burst and **0.39% / 1.15%** ending pre-burst — a coin flip against a three-minute blip. **RULED:** any alarm
  for this class is EPISODE-shaped (N rows / M sites in a T-minute window), never per-row, because a per-row
  alarm on a one-row median episode is a muted alarm within a week. The honest settled-window headline
  (25h ago → 1h ago, nothing in flight) is **745 volume / 3 failed / 254 live / 488 deferred → 0.40% on volume,
  1.17% on settled, verdict SUFFICIENT.** Two corrections ride with it: BOX_UNREACHABLE is not the only live
  failing class (four have a 24h pulse), and it has **zero Go CLI readers** — proved non-vacuous by a control
  grep on `DOC_ID_EMPTY` that DOES match.

- **D550 — THE READER-LESS INSTRUMENT CENSUS FAILS OPEN, THE REAL GATE IS A DIFFERENT FILE, AND THAT GATE HAS A
  DOCUMENTED ESCAPE ROUTE.** Proved by mutation on a clean worktree at origin/main: a probe key added to
  `census/3`'s top-level payload with no register row and no reader anywhere leaves
  `reader_less_instrument_census_test.exs` at **15 tests, 0 failures** — `@register` is a hand-typed 7-row
  literal and nothing derives the emitted key set. The safety net that DOES exist is
  `payload_key_set_census_test.exs`, which reds the same probe on two arms (`newly unread (emitted, decoded by
  NOBODY)` and the `@emitted_floor` 143→144). **THE HOLE:** the identical key emitted one level down inside the
  private helper `class_rows/3` — which really does reach the wire under `classes[]` — leaves **both** censuses
  green (38 tests, 0 failures), and `deploy_ledger.ex:1573-1581` documents that escape as a convenience it used
  deliberately. **AND A THIRD FAILURE MODE THE MODULEDOC DOES NOT NAME:** enrolling `agency` as `:has_reader`
  passes on **four PROSE lines** about a design agency in `cloud/priv/static`, certifying a key with zero code
  readers as read; declaring the same row `:stay` reds it as ROT. **RULED:** any publish-reach key is emitted at
  the TOP LEVEL of `census/3`, never inside a helper; it ships its Go reader in the same PR because the WAVE
  requires it, not because a gate can force it; and it is never named after a common English noun.

- **D551 — THE OWNER'S THIRD QUESTION, ANSWERED IN PLAIN WORDS: WIND DOWN TO A MAINTENANCE CADENCE AFTER THIS
  WAVE, CONDITIONAL ON THE COVERAGE GAUGE SHIPPING.** On this evidence the fleet already meets the bar the epic
  was opened against: 100.00% coverage on settled deferrals, 3 never-covered production rows in the corpus's
  entire history, 0.40%/1.17% on a settled 24h window, a p95 the instrument now consents to print, and zero

  connectivity blip and three singletons. **The remaining gap is DISCLOSURE, and it is one surface wide:**
  an operator on the majority path is told "deploy in progress" for ten minutes and gets exit 0. Continuing to
  run waves against this fleet would be manufacturing work, which wave 31 flagged in writing and this wave
  confirms with numbers. **THREE THINGS THE WIND-DOWN SAYS OUT LOUD, none of which were in the direction:**
  (1) the relabel IS visible and dated — 9,082 rows, 27.6% of the table, carry an anchored `409 already_running`
  under `status='failed'`, last written 2026-08-05 22:57, and the same event today mints a `deferred` row, so any
  window straddling that instant measures the taxonomy and not the fleet; (2) the abandonment path CAN lose a
  publish and has done so twice in seven firings; (3) the epic's own ledger overstates its remaining work by
  roughly a third (D546), so "N open children" is not a reason to keep running.
  **THE MAINTENANCE CADENCE IS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY DAILY:** `DailyDigestWorker` at `0 6 * * *`
  (`config.exs:334`) already calls `DeployLedger.census/3` per team and reaches a human inbox. **The epic's last
  act is to change that sentence's UNIT from the attempt to the coverage partition** — not to invent a
  scheduler, not to open a latency SLO front (p95 is 422s–1,200s on a fleet that serializes builds on ONE slot,
  reach is 100%, staleness is 0; there is no failing population there either). **If the gauge does not ship, the
  honest fallback is the pinned SQL classifier this wave commits
  (`tooling/grip/ledger/deploy-reliability-w32-classes-2026-08-09.sql`) and the recommendation still stands —
  only its mechanism downgrades.**

- **D552 — THE CLASSIFIER IS PINNED AS RUNNABLE SQL FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND IT SELF-CHECKS.**
  `tooling/grip/ledger/deploy-reliability-w32-classes-2026-08-09.sql` transliterates `classify/1`, `classify/2`
  and `classify_deferred/2` arm-for-arm in the same `cond` order, carries the w31 cohort-contract header, and
  ships its own self-check arm — settled rows with a NULL class, non-settled rows with a class, deferred rows
  leaking a failure class, failed rows leaking a deferred class — **all four returned 0**. It is a
  TRANSLITERATION, not the Elixir: it is L1 about the table and L3 about the classifier, and when the two
  disagree the Elixir is right. The file says so in its own header.

- **D553 — THE PRIMARY CHECKOUT WAS ~800 COMMITS BEHIND origin/main FOR THE WHOLE WAVE, AND IT SILENTLY REFUTED
  A TRUE CLAIM.** `grep -c seal-run .github/workflows/shell-harnesses.yml` returns 0 locally while

  exist" (it does, 1,218 lines, on origin/main) and `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/deploy_ledger.ex` "does not exist"
  (it does; and the path cited repeatedly as `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/sites/deploy_ledger.ex` has never
  existed). **STANDING RULE, elevated from advice: every file:line citation in this epic is derived with
  `git show origin/main:<path>` or it is not derived at all.** Builders run in worktrees cut from origin/main;

### WAVE 32 PLAN — SEVEN SLICES IN ROUND 1, ONE DEFERRED TO ROUND 2

The wave is deliberately cure-and-closure, not instrument-only: four of the seven round-1 slices are code
defects with a located live population, one is the exit gauge, one is a red on main, and one is the ledger
reclaim D520 forbids writing as prose.

| slice | task | surface | model | round |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The paper-publish 500 becomes a 422 that names its failures | `dr-w32-s1-ingest-wall-tuples-stop-500ing` | `api/` ingest controller | opus | 1 |
| `bp cloud site deploy` stops lying on the majority outcome | `dr-w32-s2-deferred-is-terminal-on-the-wire` | Go CLI + cloudclient | opus | 1 |
| Coverage reaches a human daily, and the failed tail stops being invisible | `dr-w32-s3-coverage-gauge-and-the-failed-tail` | `cloud/` ledger + digest | fable | 1 |
| The crown alarm stops crying wolf, in the only order that works | `dr-w32-s4-crown-alarm-speaks-then-stops-crying-wolf` | scripts + workflow | fable | 1 |
